title: Letter spacing fixed with !important
user_impact: Users cannot increase letter spacing for readability.
technical_impact: On an element with text, the style attribute sets letter-spacing with !important to less than 0.12 times the font size, so a user style sheet or bookmarklet cannot increase it for readability; a review hint when the element is out of the flow or the value cannot be resolved without layout.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.12 Text Spacing (letter spacing (tracking) at least 0.12 times the font size); CSS Cascade 4 (author !important in a style attribute); ACT 24afc2
checks.applicability: Rendered elements with text whose style attribute sets letter-spacing with !important to a value other than inherit, unset, revert or revert-layer.
checks.expectation:
Fails when that value is below 0.12 times the font size: an author declaration
with !important in the style attribute wins over every author style sheet,
including the one a text-spacing bookmarklet or extension injects, so the
letter spacing (tracking) 1.4.12 requires cannot be set. 0.1em or 2px at a
20px font fails; exactly 0.12em passes. A later declaration without !important
does not change the effective value. inherit, unset and revert take over a
value not fixed here and do not count; a value without !important can be
overridden and does not apply. When layout decides whether the text is
affected (the element or an ancestor is positioned absolute/fixed, the font
size a px value is compared with is not given in px, or for line height a
horizontally scrolling ancestor), the finding is a review, not a violation.
Text that is not rendered (display: none) is out of scope. Reported once per
element.
